course_description:
This course aims to provide final year students with the opportunity to apply conceptual knowledge to the real world via a professional placement. As such, this course strongly links discipline learnings, personal employability skills and attributes developed by students across the duration of their studies with the challenges and expectations of working in industry. In doing so, students have the opportunity to gain valuable work experience in their chosen profession and to connect this experience to the development of a workplace ready skill-set. Successful completion of the course will provide students with the employability skills required for transition to the world of work. Further information about how to apply for RBUS3999 can be found on the BEL Faculty's work-integrated learning website .

Placement/Internship requirements

Prior to enrolling in this course, you should independently secure a work placement that's relevant to your field of study. The organisation should be willing to host you, provide meaningful work that supports the development of your skills and capabilities, and appoint an experienced industry supervisor to oversee your work, provide guidance, and offer feedback on your performance. Support is available from the BEL Faculty Employability Team to help you source an appropriate host organisation.

Your industry placement (internship) should comprise between 80 and 100 hours of professional work experience, throughout (or before) the semester.ﾠAs an example, you might choose to complete your internship in one block of 3 or 4 weeks full-time,ﾠ3 days a week over 4-5 weeks, orﾠ2 days a week over 7-8 weeks.ﾠCompleting one day a week of your internship hours is notﾠrecommended as experience has shown the likelihood of you being given realistic work tasks and/or being included in the work team is significantly reduced. If completing your internship at your current employer, you must undertake higher level duties that are different from your usual role for 80-100 hours.

Domestic internships that are unpaid must be approved. All international internships must be paid

After securing your internship you need to apply for approval before you will be allowed to enrol on this course. You must complete the WIL application process, including submission of a Learning Agreement and Internship Information Form.

The course is offered four times a year to make alignment with your internship dates possible. Your internship should be as close as possible to the course start date.

If your internship commencement date is too far removed from the course start date, you may be advised to source a new internship.

NOTE: Before you commence your internship, it is important you first refer to the BEL Work-integrated Learning (WIL) website to familiarise yourself with the process of having your internship approved before it can be considered suitable for course credit. Access the BEL Internships website at my.uq.edu.au .

course_aims: This course gives students the opportunity to link discipline learnings, employability skills and personal attributes with the challenges and expectations of working in industry. It is designed to help students identify their unique strengths and build a strong professional identity. The course will reflectively deepen students’ understanding of workplace practices, processes and challenges. Ultimately, the course will help students emerge with the confidence and skills to thrive in the modern workplace.

assessment_details.task_description: In this assessment, you will showcase your reflective skills by analysing and reflecting on the business/organisation you observed and engaged with during your placement. You will critically reflect on the practices, processes, challenges and/or successes of the business or organisation you worked in. Your observations will lead you to develop a foundational understanding of how businesses operate, their managerial decision-making, and how businesses respond to wider industry/economic forces. The assessment will consist of two parts: A2.1: Written Reflection You are required to prepare a written reflection that presents your observations and critical analysis of a significant or consequential practice, process, challenge and/or opportunity within the business or organisation in which you completed your placement. Your reflection should explore the key learnings gained from this experience and explicitly connect these insights to the development of your employability skills and personal attributes. The written reflection will be submitted in two parts: Part 1 (Formative) Initial Reflection: Due Friday, 18 December 2026, at 5:00 pm and Part 2 – Final Reflection: Due Friday, 8 January 2027, at 5:00 pm. Part 2 should build upon your initial reflection (and feedback received), demonstrating deeper critical analysis and consideration of how your workplace experiences have contributed to your professional development. A2.2: Interactive Oral Assessment You will participate in a semi-structured, individual online consultation with your lecturer to discuss the significant workplace issue, practice, process, challenge or opportunity identified in A2.1. During the consultation, you will be expected to critically reflect on your experience, articulate your key learnings, and explain how these have contributed to the development of your employability skills and personal attributes. The consultation provides an opportunity to demonstrate your ability to communicate and transfer your professional learning to future workplace contexts. Assessment period: 11–29 January 2027. You will be required to book an individual consultation time with your lecturer. Booking instructions will be provided through Blackboard. Secure Assessment Materials Allowed or Prohibited You may use Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Translation (MT) tools to support your learning and assessment preparation for the written reflection and preparation for your Interactive Oral Assessment. You must transparently acknowledge any use of AI or MT. The use of AI during the Interactive Oral Assessment is not permitted. Read full task description Hide full task description

assessment_details.title: A3. Professional Development Plan
assessment_details.other_conditions: Work integrated learning. See the conditions definitions
assessment_details.task_description: In this assessment, you will develop a comprehensive and critically reflective Professional Development Plan that evaluates your employability and identifies priorities for your future professional growth. Your plan should draw on: Self-evaluation of your placement performance and professional learning. Feedback from supervisors, mentors and colleagues. Relevant self-assessment tools and instruments. Research into industry expectations, employment trends and emerging skill requirements. UQ’s graduate attributes and employability capabilities. You will identify key areas for development and establish a clear, achievable action plan with specific goals and strategies for improvement. Your plan should conclude with a critical consideration of your professional identity, career aspirations and future career pathways, demonstrating how you intend to transfer your learning from the placement into your ongoing personal and professional development. learning_activities.topic: Employ101X - Unlocking your employability This is an optional self-paced online course in which you will hear from: Employers discussing what they value when hiring new graduates Current students who have maximised their university experience Graduates who have transitioned successfully into the workplace Academics in the field of employability with insights into key topics in the course Learning outcomes: L01

Industry placement with a host organisation 80-100 hours placement with an industry host. The placement will give you the opportunity to gain valuable work experience and to connect this experience to the development of a workplace ready skill set. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L04

SEM1: Introduction to the Course This seminar will include: Course Profile Assessment overview Discover UQ WIL opportunities (Employ101x, events & workshops, employability award, etc) Discuss professionalism in the workplace Discuss agility and resilience in the workplace Learning outcomes: L01

SEM2: Reflecting on the workplace During this seminar we will Discover the value and modalities of workplace reflection. Explore potential topics/focus areas for reflection. Practice describing and analysing workplace dynamics. Learning outcomes: L01, L04

SEM3: Employability skills and attributes In this seminar we will: Differentiate between skills and attributes Explore practical ways to identify and evidence your own skills and capabilities Discover the skills and attributes most in demand by employers Understand how the UQ Graduate Attributes relate to employability Learning outcomes: L01, L02

SEM4: Professional identity and value proposition Understanding your professional self Understanding identity Personal vis a vis Professional identity Recognising your value, interests, strengths and influences Developing your professional brand and value proposition What is a brand? Why do you need a brand? Steps to building a brand. Crafting your brand statement/value proposition Learning outcomes: L01, L02

SEM5: Professional Development Plan In this seminar we will Discuss the purpose and elements of a Professional Development Plan (PDP). Consider how to identify skills and knowledge gaps and derive development areas. Explore the development of an action plan to achieve your development goals. Consider the value of a PDP in the context of your professional identity and long-term career aspirations. Learning outcomes: L01, L03
